messages:
maria.chen: Quick async check — we need a single, agreed list of who can perform an emergency toggle for the `service-toggle` feature and what metadata is required in the audit. Can we confirm who’s authorized and the exact procedure?

devon.patel: I can start — current proposal: SRE lead, Eng Platform manager, and CTO on-call can flip. Non-prod leads can only request. Toggle must include: actor, reason, incident/ticket link, and rollback window.

ashok.rao: +1 but we should scope audiences. For canary rollouts we have a separate path. Emergency toggle should always be global off for user-facing degradations. For internal feature gates (beta users) allow scoped disable.

simone.lopez: For clarity — can we list the exact Slack command or CLI we expect people to use? Need reproducible audit entries.

maria.chen: Good point. Suggested command (ops-only):
```bash
ops-toggle --feature service-toggle --action disable --actor maria.chen --reason "sev2: payment errors" --ticket INC-2026 --rollback_in 30m
```
That command should write to ops-audit and trigger deploy-bot to post in #incidents.

deploy-bot: action=toggle_request status=accepted feature=service-toggle actor=maria.chen ticket=INC-2026 trace_id=tr_8f3a

kai: Who owns the runbook step after the toggle? SRE should validate recovery steps and mark the incident as "toggle verified". Also add a short checklist in the audit: traffic checks, error-rate baseline, key downstream jobs.

devon.patel: RBAC note: only members of `ops-toggle` group and `eng-platform-admins` can run `ops-toggle` with --action disable. Others can call `ops-toggle --request` which creates an approval ticket. We should also add MFA requirement for emergency disables.

ashok.rao: Audit retention? Legal wants 1 year for anything that affects customer data. Can we make audit logs immutable once written?

maria.chen: Ops-audit will be stored in redactable-but-versioned S3 bucket with 13-month retention. Immutability via write-once keys + KMS provenance. I'll loop in security to confirm.

simone.lopez: Quick guardrail ask: automatic fallback — if toggle executed, routing must send 1% traffic back for 10m for canary verification, unless `--global` flag present. Otherwise manual rollback only.

devon.patel: Agree. We'll add `--global` explicit flag so no surprises. Default `disable` is gradual unless `--global` used. Also add a required `--postmortem` field to be filled within 72h.

maria.chen: Action items: (1) devon to PR RBAC + CLI validation (2) ashok to update runbook checklist (3) simone to add guardrail language to feature rollout doc (4) kai to own SRE verification step. I'll ping security about audit immutability. If anyone objects to the list of approvers, speak now. :eyes:

kai: ACK, will add a verification checklist in the runbook and a monitoring dashboard link.

devon.patel: I'll open PR and include example audit entry format and the deploy-bot payload schema. ETA EOD tomorrow.

ashok.rao: Fine from infra side. One more: include an escalation path (pager -> email -> exec) in case toggle doesn't help.

maria.chen: Added. Thanks all. If you need to test the flow, use the staging `ops-toggle --dry-run` which will emit a fake audit event to #eng-platform.

simone.lopez: Tested on staging, looks good. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: test_event=ops_toggle_dryrun status=ok feature=service-toggle actor=simone.lopez

maria.chen: Closing thread — I'll file a short confluence note and link PRs.
